parts.reasoning: The object is a thick, monolithic hardcover book. Assuming typical dimensions for a large reference tome (approx. 24cm x 18cm x 6cm), the volume is roughly 0.0026 cubic meters. A solid block of tightly bound paper has a density around 800 kg/m^3, resulting in an estimated mass of ~2.0 kg. The dominant external material for contact dynamics is the textured faux-leather/cloth cover. This material typically exhibits moderate friction (approx 0.4-0.5) against common surfaces like wooden desks. Because a dense stack of paper absorbs impact energy significantly, the restitution (bounciness) is estimated to be very low (0.1). For collision geometry, a bounding_cube is highly recommended as it perfectly approximates the overall rectangular prism shape of a closed book, offering the best performance for rigid body simulation. Continuous Collision Detection (CCD) is generally not required for an object of this thickness unless subjected to extreme projectile velocities.
